newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE BONDS FLAT TO HIGHER, DOWN FROM HIGHS.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE BONDS FLAT TO HIGHER, DOWN FROM HIGHS.

text.p: Argentine bonds were flat to higher late morning Wednesday after the market fell from early highs with U.S. Treasuries on the back of a weaker dollar.
"The market is moving about a lot on U.S. Treasuries," said a trader at a foreign bank.
U.S. Treasuries sprung higher early after the release of U.S. retail sale and producer price reports showing few inflationary pressures but as the dollar dipped their gains were wiped out.
Argentine players said they were keeping a close eye on the U.S. market with consumer prices and industrial production figures due out Thursday.
Argentina's Par Brady bond was up 1/8 to 73-3/8. The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was up $0.05 at 119.90.
Another trader said "floating-rate bonds are very well sustained."
Normally when interest-rate worries emerge, floating rate bonds outperform because their coupon will increase with higher rates.
